thread:
mike_infra: Heads-up — planning a tf apply for hybrid routing + NAT scaling tied to release v1.9. Change window 02:00-03:00 UTC (overnight). I have a plan ready and state locked locally. @olivia_sre can you watch the health checks? :eyes:

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for workspace=prod, summary: +3 resources, ~2 changed. Plan file: gs://redwood-tf-plans/prod/1839001122.plan :white_check_mark:

olivia_sre: reading now. I'll put the oncall into monitor. Can you paste the specific modules you intend to touch?

mike_infra: modules: module.networking.module.hybrid_routing, module.networking.module.nat_gateway_autoscale, module.iam.role-routing. Also will pin provider aws to 4.60.0 in the module overrides to avoid the new provider behavior.

jenna_platform: +1 on pinning provider. We saw drift with 4.62 last month. Add the provider pin to the tfvars or overrides so Dedicated doesn't pick up newer provider on apply.

alex_neteng: quick check — does this change affect any TGW attachments or route propagation? Need to ensure existing TGW routes aren't briefly removed.

mike_infra: Good call. The plan shows route additions and a replacement for nat gateway resource (scaling). No TGW detach. I'll add continue_only if plan indicates a replace on route tables.

olivia_sre: I'll set up synthetic traffic to the egress endpoints at 01:50 UTC and watch 5-min error rates. If we see >5% 5m error rate, we'll hit rollback.

mike_infra: apply steps: 1) run terraform apply -auto-approve -parallelism=10 2) watch deploy-bot logs and cloudwatch alarms 3) verify egress connectivity 4) enable scaled down nodes removal. If something goes wrong — rollback = apply previous state from snapshot: `gsutil cp gs://redwood-tf-state-backups/prod/state-1838999999.tfstate ./terraform.tfstate && terraform apply -auto-approve`

deploy-bot: starting terraform apply at 1839001400 UTC. Lock acquired: dynamodb-table=redwood-tf-locks-prod. Streaming output...

deploy-bot: 
```
module.nat_gateway_autoscale.aws_nat_gateway.main: Modifying... (ID: nat-0a1b2c3d)
  allocation_id: "eipalloc-12345" => "eipalloc-12345"
  tags.%: "3" => "4"
module.hybrid_routing.aws_route.route_to_tgw: Creating...
Apply complete! Resources: 1 added, 2 changed, 0 destroyed.
```

olivia_sre: Seeing a blip in outbound connections around +4s, 200->503 spike for 20s then recovered. Monitoring OK now. :white_check_mark:

alex_neteng: Verified no TGW flaps. Route propagation steady.

jenna_platform: Did we update the provider pin? Confirm commit hash/version so we don't drift on next release.

mike_infra: Provider pin committed in release branch: `terraform { required_providers { aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 4.60.0" } } }`. Pushed and tagged: refs/tags/release-v1.9-infra-apply-1839001122.

olivia_sre: All checks green. We'll let this sit in canary for 30m. If nothing else, we'll promote to full rollout for other regions at 02:40 UTC.

jenna_platform: Add note to release notes: "Pinned AWS provider to 4.60.0 to ensure stable TGW/route behavior; scaled NAT GW autoscaling added for egress capacity."

mike_infra: If we see sustained >2m errors or TGW detach, rollback plan: revert tag and run `terraform apply -target=module.hybrid_routing -var='force_replace=true'` or restore state snapshot as last resort. I'll be on pager for next hour.

olivia_sre: Thanks — I also bumped synthetic frequency to 1m and will escalate to oncall if errors persist.

alex_neteng: FYI I'll open a short postmortem template if we need rollback (pre-populated runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runbooks/infra-apply).

mike_infra: Closing thread after canary window. Tagging archive when full rollout completes. :shipit:
